references.text: Aaron and his sons must follow the regulations to avoid incurring guilt and dying when they enter the tent of meeting.
The continuation of the command to wash, emphasizing that this is a permanent statute for the priests.
Moses placed the bronze basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and feet there before entering the tent or approaching the altar.
Moses washed Aaron and his sons with water as part of the consecration ritual for the priesthood.
Aaron must bathe his body in water before putting on the holy garments and performing service.
The Levites must be careful not to come too near the holy objects or the altar, otherwise they will die.
David speaks of washing his hands in innocence before going around the Lord's altar, as a parallel to the priests' cleansing.
We shall draw near with a sincere heart and full assurance of faith, having our hearts cleansed from a guilty conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
Direct fulfillment: Describes how the priests actually performed the washing as commanded in 30:20.
